title: Porsche Design System deprecation audit report (js)

runId.description: Filesystem-safe UTC timestamp identifying the run, e.g. 2026-07-23T09-21-27Z.

auditKind.description: What this report audits, for a consumer reading a run directory of several.

pdsVersion.description: The installed PDS version the audit was run against.

scope.description: What the run covered, as a list rather than as a claim about the file walk. A package that was never discovered is a package nobody can see was missed, so `completed` is checked against these two arrays.

includedPaths.description: Every path the run audited, project-relative: one entry per discovered PDS-dependent package root, narrowed by any user-supplied include paths. `.` when the project is a single package.

excludedPaths.description: Every path deliberately left out, each with why — user-supplied excludes, default exclusions such as tests or build output, and any discovered package the run chose not to audit. A choice belongs here and not in `coverage.limitations`, which is for what the audit could not do.

summary.description: Execution state and nothing else. Counts are deliberately absent: each one would be the length of an array in this same file, and a written number is a number that can disagree with the list beside it.

result.description: Execution state only, never project quality: completed = every discovered PDS-dependent package audited and every eligible file in it checked; partial = a discovered package went unaudited or something eligible could not be checked; failed = no meaningful audit was possible.

coverage.description: Deliberately thin. Anything here is the audit grading its own work, which no consumer can check, so it carries only what a reader can act on: paths they can open, and gaps stated in words. Without it a `partial` result names no gap at all.

limitations.description: Anything that prevented a complete check, disclosed in full. Only what the audit could not do — anything it chose to leave out is a decision and belongs in `scope.excludedPaths` with its reason.

findings.description: Every deprecated usage found, ordered cheapest first: effective effort ascending, then confidence, then occurrence count descending, then ruleId. That order is the recommended action plan.

ruleId.description: The deprecation index entry id, e.g. prop/p-accordion/heading, copied verbatim. Stable across releases, so findings stay comparable between runs.

title.description: One line naming the deprecated API, e.g. "Deprecated prop heading on p-accordion".

deprecationMessage.description: The index entry’s message, carried verbatim when it has one.

confidence.description: Derived, not judged: the lowest confidence across this finding’s evidence locations.

baselineEffort.description: Derived from usageKind, one level higher when the index documents no replacement.

observedEffort.description: Only when this project implements the API in a way that changes the real cost.

effortRationale.description: Required whenever observedEffort is present, and must point at evidence already listed on this finding — otherwise the deviation is unreviewable.

replacement.description: The exact edit, in this framework’s spelling. Present only when the index documents an unambiguous replacement, so a fix never has to re-derive it from prose.

instruction.description: What to do, in words. When no replacement is documented, say so plainly rather than inventing one.

line.description: The usage itself — the attribute, tag, property or alias reference. Never the import, @use, @theme or declaration line that anchored or resolved it: those belong in `anchor`, and counting them as locations makes two runs of the same project disagree on how many there are.

detection.description: How this location was reached. Determines its confidence.

valueResolution.description: How the deprecated value was resolved. Only for usageKind `propValue`.

line.description: The anchoring line, which is frequently in a different file from the usage.

anchor.description: The line that proves this usage is PDS — the import, the resolved SCSS @use including one injected by build config, the Tailwind @theme import, or the PDS root at the far end of a wrapper chain. The only truthful home for the vite.config.ts line that anchors a stylesheet naming PDS nowhere. Omitted only when the usage anchors itself, as a --p- custom property does.

sources.description: Where the fact came from, so a reader or a fix skill can re-ground the finding.

reference.description: Knowledge-skill reference the fact comes from, as a path relative to that skill’s root — the same form the knowledge skill uses for its own links, so a consumer can resolve it without guessing the base directory.

manualFollowUps.description: Deprecated usage that was detected but could not be resolved. Kept apart from findings because a follow-up has no fix to apply — anything acting on this report leaves these to a human.

subject.description: What could not be resolved, e.g. "p-text size". Free text, since a follow-up often spans several index entries.

ruleId.description: Only when the follow-up maps to exactly one index entry, and then copied verbatim. Omit it rather than inventing one: an id that is not in the index cannot be looked up or compared across runs.

reason.description: Why it could not become a finding — dynamic value, unanchored match, spread props.
